official.english_requirement: No scholarship-specific English test is published on the Killam page; the Faculty of Graduate Studies admission minimums apply to the PhD program: IELTS Academic 7; TOEFL iBT 92 for tests taken before January 21, 2026, or overall 4.5 on the 1-6 score scale for tests taken on or after January 21, 2026; CAEL 70 with no band below 60; PTE Academic overall 65 with nothing below 54; MET 64 with no skills area below 53; or completion of Dalhousie's English for Academic Purposes Level 2 course with an overall grade of A-. The requirement can be waived for applicants who completed a degree at a recognized university where the language of instruction is English in a country where English is an official language; some programs require higher scores.

applicant_utility.summary: Killam is Dalhousie's flagship doctoral stipend and is worth pursuing alongside a Tri-agency CGRS-D application, because filing a CGRS-D through Dalhousie puts you into the Killam pool automatically, and winning the CGRS-D actually lifts your combined support to $48,000 a year. Non-Tri-agency applicants compete through the FGS Scholarship Management Platform, with round one closing October 16, 2026 and round two closing January 31, 2027, and every eligible file is judged in one pool with offers emailed by May 15, 2027. The award is income support plus a relocation travel reimbursement, not tuition relief, so doctoral tuition and fees still need a separate plan. Mind the time-in-program clock: the award must be taken up by your 7th term and you must be under six terms (24 months) into the PhD as of May 1 of the award year.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving Dalhousie doctoral students, especially those in their first two PhD years who can also compete for a Tri-agency CGRS-D, including international students content to study in Canada.

common_rejection_risks: Submitting more than one application - duplicates are disqualified outright
Being too advanced in the PhD: the award must be taken up by the 7th term and you must be under six terms (24 months) in the program as of May 1 of the award year
Assuming Killam stacks fully with other awards - it becomes partially or fully honorary in terms where a CGRS-D, DRES or Abdul Majid Bader scholarship is also held
Missing the July 31 annual report deadline, which is a standing condition of holding the award

applicant_utility.summary: DRES is an entrance award built for people about to begin a Dalhousie PhD between January 2027 and January 2028, so it fits applicants still finalising their doctoral destination rather than students already well into a programme. The $35,000 a year is a split package, not a single cheque: $28,000 comes from Graduate Studies and $7,000 from your supervisor or programme, so the strength of your supervisor's funding matters as much as your record. Nothing in the award pays tuition, and the money is only administered after you are admitted and registered, so treat it as income layered on a funding package you still have to assemble. If you also win a Killam the two combine to $42,000 a year, while a CGRS-D makes the DRES honorary as you draw the $40,000 tri-agency value.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong prospective PhD applicants choosing Dalhousie for a January 2027 to January 2028 start, especially those with publications, a leadership track record and a well-funded supervisor.

common_rejection_risks: Intended PhD start date outside the January 2027 - January 2028 window
Assuming the award is guaranteed money - it is administered only after admission and registration, so an admission failure ends it
Submitting multiple applications across rounds or categories; only one per candidate is reviewed
Transferring from a master's to a PhD before applying for the doctoral scholarship, which forfeits consideration because time-in-program runs from the effective transfer date
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Doctoral tuition and fees, relocation and travel costs (no relocation allowance is published for DRES), and living costs beyond the stipend, including exposure if the supervisor's $7,000 share is not secured.

For master's-to-PhD transfers, expect the timing of the transfer to matter because eligibility and time-in-program run from the effective transfer date
